rules.sentence: In 1912, Allen B. Kanavel described 3 cardinal signs of pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis: flexor sheath tenderness, flexed position of the affected digit, and painful passive digital extension.
Later, a fourth sign, fusiform swelling of the digit, was also added to become the 4 cardinal signs.[4]

Objectives: Identify the cardinal signs of pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis, including flexor sheath tenderness, flexed positioning of the affected digit, painful passive digital extension, and fusiform swelling.

Implement timely and effective management strategies for pyogenic flexor tenosynovitis, emphasizing surgical washout and other urgent interventions crucial for preserving viable and functioning fingers.
